newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC falls as investors pull out profit.
newsitem.headline: CITIC falls as investors pull out profit.

text.p: Shares of conglomerate CITIC Pacific Ltd fell on Friday on profit-taking after a recent rally, brokers said.
"Investors took profit after they saw limited room on the upside after the recent rally," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
CITIC shares were off HK$1.80 or 3.99 percent at HK$43.30 at the mid-session break on volume of 11.26 million shares worth HK$493.88 million, topping the most actively traded list.
The shares had risen HK$4.60 or 11.41 percent last month.

"The parent selling CITIC shares to the management has triggered worries of possible future share placement and investors took the dilution fear as an excuse to take profit," a sales director at a local brokerage said.

CITIC said on Monday that a management team headed by chairman Larry Yung would buy a 15.47 percent stake in the company at HK$33 per share from parent China International Trust and Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd.
Brokers said they expected CITIC shares to remain volatile in the short run, although the downside was seen as limited due to the current strong market sentiment for red chips.
